# Workflow spec reference

## Contents

- Top level
- Start methods (`trigger`)
- Steps
- Branch operators
- Scoping rules
- Text that takes merges
- Checked against Docusign's help (2026-10-28)

This is the reference for spec authors writing `assets/workflows/specs/<id>.json`. It lists every key
the compiler (`src/workflow-spec.ts`) reads. The process is in
[WORKFLOW-AUTHORING.md](WORKFLOW-AUTHORING.md). How each shape was learned is in
[WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md](WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md). What Docusign's builder offers is in
[WORKFLOW-BUILDER-GUIDE.md](WORKFLOW-BUILDER-GUIDE.md).

**The compiler refuses any key it does not read.** An unknown step, a mistyped option or an extra
key is an error that names its place (`steps[1].then[0] (confirm): unknown key "body" — allowed:
title, description`). Before 2026-10-24 such keys were silently dropped.

**Proven** says how far each item has been proven on the legacy lab account:

- **RUN**: a published copy ran end to end (WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md "Running a workflow end to end",
  "Running a workflow through the public API").
- **import**: a library spec that uses it passed all five gates of `captures/workflow-verify.ts`
  (validate, import, rewire, canvas, cleanup). The report is committed in `assets/workflows/verify/`.
- **lab**: a lab probe passed the five gates, but the probe and its report are not committed
  (WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md "Coverage").
- **harvest**: the shape was built in the builder and read back. The compiler writes the same
  shape, but no gate has run on that exact use.
- **—**: compiled, never proven.

## Top level

| Key | Meaning | Proven |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | file name; seeds every id in the package | RUN |
| `name` | the workflow's name | RUN |
| `description` | the workflow's description | import |
| `summary` | the gallery tile's text; never compiled | — |
| `trigger` | how it starts (below); a link when absent | — |
| `participants` | `[{ role, name, email, phone? }]`: the people beyond the starter (`phone`: `start.<a Phone starting variable>`, for a text-message invite or signing link). `name`/`email` are each a form answer `<form>.<field>`, a starting value `start.<name>`, a Read from Salesforce output `<as>.<field>` (the opportunity's contact role: `contact.Contact.Email` from an OpportunityContactRole read `by: OpportunityId`), under a request start a request text field `C_…` (INFERRED until lab `zz-generate-record-from-request` runs), or a fixed value | RUN (form, fixed, start value; a Salesforce read as a send's signer 2026-10-31, [report](../assets/workflows/live/nda-signed-filed-on-opportunity-run.json)) |
| `steps` | the steps, in order | — |
| `instanceName` | "Name instances" at publish: text with at most 3 `{{x}}` merges (`run.startDate`, `run.instanceId`, `start.<name>`, a request field), stored as the definition's `instanceName` editor document. Merges must be text, number, date, email, phone or Boolean values (help); the custom name applies only once an instance COMPLETES — in progress, canceled or failed instances keep the system name ([iqm1698272226447](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=yff1696971835267&topicId=iqm1698272226447.html)) | — (key from a published definition, 2026-10-26) |

`starter` names whoever started the workflow. Under an Event, Schedule, CLM or automated API start
there is no starter, so every participant needs an `invite` first.

Insights available: ONE condition (the builder offers no AND / OR there) on a Navigator agreement property key (`AgreementType` option key, `TotalContractValueCurrency` a number in USD, …). The request type is carried in the package. **Anything that references Salesforce starts from Salesforce** (2026-10-28): a workflow that
reads a Salesforce record starts from the launcher (From a Link / From an API Call, human) and reads the
launching record (`start.recordId`). A person never types a Salesforce id; the compiler refuses one.

**Salesforce → request → workflow (pattern, 2026-10-28).** A workflow started by an Agreement
Desk request (`"trigger": { "request": "<type>" }`: the request-submitted event filtered to that type)
gets that type's intake answers as variables (`C_…`, provisions), plus the request's own. So data flows
through the request: W1, started from the Salesforce launcher, creates the request (Create a Request, the
Opportunity id mapped from `start.recordId` into a read-only intake field); W2, started by that request,
branches on the intake answers, runs request approvals and statuses, and generates the Salesforce order
form from the read-only id field. RUN-PROVEN on the lab account (2026-10-28, labs `zz-w1-create-request` +
`zz-w2-request-started`, W2 run c6e14f1a): the request W1's interactive Create a Request made (crm_id
read-only = 006bm00000a0IcvAAE from `start.recordId`) was submitted and STARTED W2, which set its status
and read `C_IntakeCrmId` (the id is in its message). With the external source set (second chain run,
2026-10-28, report captures/deploy-default/request-chain/2026-10-28T16-32-27-844Z) the request carries
Salesforce / Opportunity / 006bm00000a0IcvAAE / the org and a link to the Opportunity ("View in
Salesforce"), and W2 read it as `TicketObjectId` ("Request Object Id") — RUN-PROVEN, so the library pair
`sales-contract-request-from-opportunity` (W1) + `deal-approval-on-request` (W2) uses that and no typed or
mapped id. Deploy order: W1 CARRIES the request type (the importer
re-points a Create a Request's `requestTypeId` only to a carried type); W2 names it with the build option
`existingRequestTypes` (its trigger compares the type's name).

**Started from Salesforce (the Docusign IAM Launcher; "Opportunity Launcher" is our name for it):** an API start (human) or a Link start whose variables are exactly the
four Docusign's help names, all Text: `recordId`, `objectName`, `applicationName`, `orgId`
([Workflow Builder for Salesforce](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=qwr1706590641805&topicId=tskccafc250-9431-4f0c-9518-d4526d9128b1.html)).
the owner's rule (2026-10-28): these four, no fewer (Docusign's own launcher samples use three; not allowed
here), started by a human: From a Link (a user clicks) or From an API Call (an API call or the Salesforce
Flow action). Declaring any of them makes the compiler require all four; `automated` is refused. 

**Started from a Salesforce Flow** ([help ovh1741282680990](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=qwr1706590641805&topicId=ovh1741282680990.html); 2026-10-28): a record-triggered Flow (e.g. on Opportunity, record updated) with the **Start Docusign
Workflow** action — Instance Name, Workflow ID, Record ID (the record's id), Variable 1…N — starts the
workflow with no click. Spec: `"trigger": { "api": { "variables": [...], "automated": true, "salesforce":
{ "object": "Opportunity", "via": "flow" } } }`. Required: the Text variable `Record ID` (case sensitive) and
the four launcher variables (Salesforce passes those too); optional `Variable 1` … `Variable 9` (at most ten
Flow variables, exact names, Text). The help recommends From an API Call with "Automated process", so
`automated` is allowed here (and only here). A Salesforce template reads `start.recordId`, as under the
launcher. HARVESTED from the account's own "sf Flow Workflow" (cd2949d4, read 2026-10-28): the trigger is
`type: 'API', httpType: 'Post'` (Automated), and each variable — `Record ID_<trigger>` with path
`["Record ID"]`, `Variable 1…5`, and the four — is keyed exactly as the compiler writes it (the compiled
payload and output key sets match the export's). Lab `zz-flow-start-salesforce` imports and passes the
canvas and the builder's ready-to-publish check (2026-10-28). RUN-PROVEN 2026-10-29 (lab
`sales-contract-request-from-flow`, runs dc0140f4 and b789a328, Flow `ZZ_Lab_Send_to_Docusign` from
captures/sf-flow-demo.ts): ticking an Opportunity checkbox started it with nobody at a keyboard. The run's
inputs held `Record ID` AND the four launcher variables (`recordId`, `objectName` = Opportunity,
`applicationName` = Salesforce, `orgId`) and `Variable 1`; it started as the account's connected Docusign
user. Its Read from Salesforce steps read `start.recordId`, and an AUTOMATIC Create a Request made the
request with the Opportunity as its external source (View in Salesforce) and every mapped field filled; that
creation starts a request-started workflow on the type (`submitted`), as an interactive submit does. The
Salesforce action is the package's `dfsle__TriggerWorkflowRequest` (inputs `instanceName`, `workflowId`,
`recordId`, `variable1` … `variable9`). The start also names the ONE object it is
launched from, `"salesforce": { "object": "Opportunity" }` inside `trigger.api`: `recordId` is that
object's id (`objectName` says which). The launcher, the **Start with Docusign** action ([help](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=qwr1706590641805&topicId=tsk32e505bf-436a-47b1-b7f6-55e6ad614ec5.html); the
**Docusign IAM Launcher** component, [help](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=qwr1706590641805&topicId=tsk590e18e7-9dbc-418f-9fb8-0169f182eb3a.html)), must be placed on that object's page layout; in our org
its label is "Start Agreement Process". A `generate` of a Salesforce-bound template requires that object to
be the template's root (its spec's `salesforce.object`; otherwise the error names both), and `"recordId":
"start.recordId"`.

| Library spec | Launched from (place the launcher on) |
|---|---|
| `deal-approval-matrix` | Opportunity |
| `opportunity-order-form` | Opportunity |
| `nda-filed-on-opportunity` | Opportunity |
| `nda-signed-filed-on-opportunity` | Opportunity |

A starting value is `start.<name>`: an API or CLM variable, or an event's envelope property
(`SenderName`, `SenderEmail`, `Subject`, `EnvelopeId`, …). You can use one wherever a form answer
can go.

## Steps

Every step also takes `name` (the step's name on the canvas).

| Step | Keys | Docusign step | Proven |
|---|---|---|---|
| `form` | `form` (library web form id), `by` (participant; starter by default), `prefill` { text field: text with `{{…}}` values from earlier steps } (the drawer's Map data fields; harvest 2026-11-01, unproven) | Collect Data with Web Forms | RUN (`prefill`: not yet) |
| `generate` | `generate` (library document template), `fill` { field: source }, `hideForm`, `reviewerCanEdit: false` ("Allow reviewer to edit" off: stored as allowReviewerToEditSenderFields false with the form hidden; every required field must be filled; harvest 2026-11-01, unproven), `unattended: true` (under an automated API start, a request-submitted start or a request status-changed start: no participant, no preview, the form hidden; under a request or status start the document lands on the request's Documents tab ([status-start lab run](../assets/workflows/live/status-start-unattended-run.json), 2026-11-01), where `getDocument` collects it — RUN 2026-10-31, [report](../assets/workflows/live/gym-membership-on-request-run.json) — the step generates by itself, as Docusign's own "Fontara Renewal Order Form" package stores it; every required field must be filled; RUN 2026-10-31, [report](../assets/workflows/live/gym-membership-from-signup-run.json); a later send to a participant still needs their Set Up Invite first), `by` (a participant holding the step must sign in to Docusign: a zz-lab invitee with no account got "Log in to Docusign" from the invite link, lab 2026-11-01; `workflow:check` warns — hold it by an account user, or send an `esign` template to outside people), `format` (`docx` default, or `pdf`), `recordId` (a Salesforce template only, and required there. Rule (2026-10-28): anything that references Salesforce starts from Salesforce; a person never types a Salesforce id. Three forms: `start.recordId` under the launcher's API start with `salesforce.object` = the template's root; or, under a request start, a READ-ONLY request field (`C_…`, `readOnly: true` in the request-type spec) that the launcher-started workflow's Create a Request filled from `start.recordId` — run-proven reading a request field (run a566baff). Or, under a request start, `TicketObjectId` ("Request Object Id"): the request's external source, which a launcher-started workflow's Create a Request sets from the launch (objectId ← `start.recordId`, objectName, applicationName, thirdPartyAccountId ← `orgId`; the request then shows "View in Salesforce") — Docusign's own MSA sample maps "Opportunity ID = Request Object Id"; run-proven 2026-10-28. A typable field is refused. Its Salesforce fields fill from that record and may not be in `fill`; stored as the export's `recordIdMapping`), `documentName` (a custom title, ≤3000; `{{x}}` merges compile to the Title Builder's document with a mention, as Docusign's own export stores it — lab 9a73fad9's drawer shows it; the product joins parts with "_"; a request attachment still takes the template's name) | Prepare Document Template. A source is `<form>.<field>`, `start.<name>`, `run.startDate` (date fields only) or `<agent>.<output>` (text). `hideForm` is refused while a required field is unfilled. A template dropdown takes only a form dropdown whose options it all has. Even with `hideForm` the step is the STARTER's: the run waits until the starter opens the run's link (an API start's `instance_url`), where Next advances it. With `by` (an invited participant, the shape under an automated start) the invitee's invite link opens that preview instead (ciiaa-from-hris run 2026-10-30: invite → preview with the start values filled → Next → creator send to the invitee) | RUN (form answers, run.startDate; and 2026-10-25 start values into text and number fields, with `hideForm`); import (agent); harvest (dropdowns) |
| `esign` | `esign` (library eSignature template) or { `fromAccount`: <the target account's template id, or its exact name (resolved at deploy: exactly one template must have it)>, `signers` [{ `role`, `tabs`? }] }, `fill` { tab: source } | Prepare eSignature Template. Text tabs, plus empty number tabs by label: `PaymentAmount` on a template whose payment is `"per-envelope"`, or the number tabs a computed payment (`"amount": { "formula": … }`) reads (from a number, currency or dropdown answer or a Salesforce number field; written locked; the drawer shows them, see below); empty email tabs by label, from a form email field (drawer harvest 2026-11-01; compiled, not yet run). A radio group takes a web form radio answer, by the group's name (`fill` { `Financing`: `<form>.<radio>` }; the form's options must be the group's values, each value equal to its text; import + drawer proven 2026-11-01, [live record](../assets/prompt-corpus/live/re-offer-proof-of-funds-run.json); a run needs a person to submit the form). A checkbox tab is refused: the drawer does not offer one; not `run.startDate` (it prints raw). A tab takes a form answer, `start.x`, an agent output, a Salesforce read or lookup output (`<as>.<field>`: the drawer's variable picker lists Read from Salesforce ▸ Opportunity / Name; run 2026-10-30, the envelope's customer tab read "Pine Care — Renewal Order Form"), or under a request start a request field (C_… or TicketTitle; run 2026-10-30, envelope tabs "ZZ Owner Value" and the request title). The importer must CREATE the step's template from the package: naming an account template without carrying it is refused (400 ERR_13004 "Failed to create eSign template", lab 2026-10-30) — the compiler refuses `{ template }`; the way round is re-pointing the step to the original in the builder after import. `fromAccount`: the deploy reads that template by REST (with its documents) and carries a COPY, which the workflow uses; the original is untouched. `signers` names its roles and the tabs `fill` uses, checked against the template at deploy; built without the account (CI, gallery) nothing is carried and `workflow:check` warns. **The step's drawer**: it lists the fills from its config instance, keyed by the template tab's tabId. The compiler fills that map, and gives each carried tab the page and x/y the account will give it (recorded by `captures/esign-tab-positions.ts`). An import re-keys the map only when those match exactly. Without recorded positions, the drawer shows the fills empty. They still run, but saving that drawer clears them and unlocks every tab (lab 2026-10-31, [live report](../assets/workflows/live/esign-drawer-fills.json)); `workflow:check` warns. A number tab fill (`PaymentAmount`, or a number a payment formula reads) is in the map too, as the variable's key itself (`"fee_<step>"`, not an editor document; drawer harvest 2026-10-31): the drawer shows it, a drawer Save keeps it, and a run after the Save filled it ([live report](../assets/workflows/live/esign-number-fill-drawer.json)) | RUN (library); drawer map: deploy, drawer, save and run 2026-10-31; `fromAccount`: see the capability row |
| `sign` | `sign` { template role: participant } (a signer, a field-less role listed in `copies`, or an eSignature template's Receives a Copy role — each of those must be named; harvest 2026-11-01, unproven. Refused: an eSignature template's Needs to View role, which the drawer offers but a run leaves out of the envelope, and any template with an in-person signer or witness, which a run cannot send; runs 2026-10-31, [live report](../assets/workflows/live/send-envelope-viewer-run.json)), `subject`, `message`, `sender` (`starter` default, or `creator`; with `documents` under a request start also `submitter` or `owner`: the request's submitter / owner sends, as 'Change default sender' offers — the builder's fixed participants, config senderType agreementDeskRequestSubmitter / …Owner, harvest B4-S2; **Request starts, runs 2026-10-29 (a2 run 1bd3c72e, ZZ Lab chain runs):** the run gets a CUSTOM dropdown as its bare option value (`C_IntakeDealSize_…: "Over_1000000_USD"`). It has no `_selected`, so a rule on the field's "(Option text)" read nothing and was always false. The compiler now compares the bare field with the option's value; the spec still names the option label. A provision dropdown (PaymentTerms) does carry `_selected` {value, label}. The trigger's Request Owner is empty for a new request, so an approval to `owner` failed BadRequest. After the workflow's own `owner: submitter` step, `owner` compiles to the submitter. While a Set Up Invite waits, its history shows `participantEmail: ""`. That is normal: the invite email was delivered (lab inbox, fixed address and request-field bindings both).

A **Who** is `"submitter"` or `"owner"`, or `{ "user": "<email>" }` / `{ "group": "<name>" }` (resolved
against the target account; a package naming one is for that account), or `{ "user": "presenter" }` (whoever
loads or deploys the workflow: a step the presenter acts on live, e.g. software-purchase-review's approval), or, for a message only,
`{ "email": "…" }`. A message to a group is refused (a product limit): Send Message from a Request takes users and email
addresses only, and a stored group fails to open the step (acceptance 6, bug 19; harvest 2026-11-02;
`request-type.automation.send-message-group`). A message's user is stored as the builder stores a picked one
(`participantId`, `type: "User"`); library spec `legal-process-legal-ops-alert` verified on a second lab account 2026-11-02 (`request-type.automation.send-message-user`). Built without the account's directory (CI, the gallery's portable package) a user or group
compiles to a placeholder id (`directory:user:<email>` / `directory:group:<name>`) and `workflow:check` warns.
A directory holds the account's real ids: a made-up user or group id (`00000000-…`, one character repeated) is refused.
Deploy and `workflow-verify` read the account's directory and write the real ids; `--user-alias=<spec email>=<account email>` maps a spec's placeholder person to an account user, and the package then carries that user's own id, name and email (before 2026-10-31 it kept the placeholder email). The importer does NOT re-map
a user or group by name: a package with another account's group id imports and reviews clean but keeps that id
(lab 43dd3853, 2026-10-30). The built-in groups `Administrators` and `Everyone` exist in every account. A Who cannot be a workflow value (a lookup, agent or form output): the Approvers picker offers only "Pick a user or group" and, under Variables from Workflow Start, Request Owner and Request Submitter (drawer, lab 2026-10-30); the compiler refuses `<as>.<field>` there. Route with a branching rule that names each person, or message the looked-up person.

**Request-start steps** (`owner`, `status`, `due`, `approval`, `followers`, `message`, `permission`,
`changeTitle`, `getDocument`) need a `request` or `statusChanged` trigger.

**Status colours by meaning** (2026-11-25). A status names a stage, not a verdict: the red/yellow/green verdict goes in the request's title, message and owner, so a red paper waiting with legal is *In Legal Review* in blue, not red. Pick the colour by what the stage means. The one source is `assets/request-types/status-colors.json` (its `statuses` list names every status the library uses); the table below is generated from it (`npx tsx src/status-colors.ts`):

<!-- status-colors:start -->
| Color | Meaning | Example statuses | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grey (`neutral`) | Not started yet, or closed with nothing wrong | New, Draft, Closed, Cancelled | Nothing to do yet, or nothing left to do: grey draws no attention. |
| Blue (`blue`) | Our side is working on it (any review, triage or drafting) | In Progress, In Legal Review, Business Review, In Review – Finance | Work in progress is normal, not a warning: In Legal Review is a stage, whatever the paper's verdict. |
| Orange (`warning`) | Waiting for an approver's decision | Pending Approval, Awaiting Approval | Someone named has to decide; Docusign's own Pending Approval is orange. |
| Purple (`purple`) | Waiting on someone outside: the counterparty, signers or a vendor | Waiting on Counterparty, Waiting for Signature, Sent for Signature | The ball is in another court; nobody inside can move it. |
| Green (`success`) | Good to go, or done | Ready to Finalize, Ready for Signature, Approved, Completed | Green reads as approved or finished, so only those stages get it (not New). |
| Red (`alert`) | Stopped, sent back, or needs attention now | Renewal Declined, Rejected, Escalated to VP, Hold Notice Urgent, Notice Clock Running | Red reads as rejected, blocked or urgent, so a normal review never gets it. |
<!-- status-colors:end -->

Docusign's own Get Started statuses do not follow this (New green, In Progress orange, Legal Review and Business Review grey, Waiting for Signature red); the lab accounts are recoloured to the rule, and the Agreements app's Account setup recolours an SC's account. `gold`, `cactus`, `maroon` and `teal` are not used. test/status-colors.test.ts pins every library, seed and prompt-corpus status to the file (corpus specs a live run pins by hash keep their colours until their next live run).

## Branch operators

| Field | Operators the spec writes | What the product offers (guide jaf1716918359288) |
|---|---|---|
| form text or radio answer, request text, starting text (type String/Email) | `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `notStartsWith`, `endsWith`, `notEndsWith`, `empty: true`, `notEmpty: true`; `matchCase: true` on any of the value comparisons (lab 5/5 for is/contains/notStartsWith/empty; harvest for the rest) | Equal to, Not equal to, Contains, Does not contain, Ends with, Does not end with, Starts with, Does not start with, Is empty, Is not empty; Match casing |
| form dropdown/radio, request choice | `is` with one of the field's option TEXTS (checked) | equals an option |
| agent number output (Float), starting Number | `gt`, `lt`, `gte`, `lte`; `is` / `isNot` with a number (Equal to / Not equal to: the numeric rules' shape with Equal / NotEqual, inferred, then import-, canvas- and review-proven: library spec `leave-request-routing`, the lab account 2026-11-02) | numeric comparisons, empty checks |
| form Number | `gt`, `lt`, `gte`, `lte`, and `is` / `isNot` with a number (inferred, as above), on its "(Normalized)" Float (lab 5/5 for the four) | Equal to, Not equal to, >, <, ≥, ≤, Is empty, Is not empty |
| form Currency | `gt`, `lt`, `gte`, `lte` on its "(Double Value)" Float (`<key>.doubleValue`). The builder declares a Currency field as `<key>` (Currency), `<key>.doubleValue` and `<key>.currencyCode` (lab `zz-form-currency-outputs`, 2026-10-26). The earlier `.normalized` operand evaluated FALSE for $5.3M in a live run; it was only ever read back from our own outputs. Run probe: `zz-currency-run-probe` | as Number |
| form Date | `is`, `isNot`, `gte` ("Is on or after"), `lte` ("Is on or before") a "YYYY-MM-DD" (UTC midnight), or `today` / `empty` / `notEmpty: true` (lab 5/5 except isNot / empty / notEmpty: harvest) | Is, Is not, Is on or before, Is on or after, Is today, Is empty, Is not empty — static dates only |
| request provision dropdown (`PaymentTerms`) | `is` / `isNot` with one of its option TEXTS (checked), on its "(Option text)" Enum, stored with no caseSensitive (builder harvest, lab 079ad69e on the lab account, 2026-10-28) | Payment terms (Option text) / (API value), with the text operator list |
| request custom NUMBER or CURRENCY field (`C_IntakeDiscount`, `C_IntakeContractAmount`) | `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `is`, `isNot` with a number: a Number compared as itself (Float), a Currency by its amount (`<field>.doubleValue`, "[Currency Value] <label>"); the compiler declares them on the start the builder's way. Proven 2026-10-31 on a second lab account ([live report](../assets/workflows/live/request-number-branch-run.json)): $1,003.25 went the ELSE way on > 5000 and the THEN way on > 1000; a quantity of 102 THEN on ≥ 10, ELSE on ≥ 1000. Library specs `contract-value-over-threshold` (the help's "Total Contract Value > $5,000") and `equipment-purchase-approval-threshold`. The earlier text-only finding (lab zz-reprobe-request-steps, 2026-10-28) came from a start that declared them as text | number operators |
| request value provision (`TotalValue`, spec key `ContractValue`) | the same, by its amount (`TotalValue_<…>.doubleValue`, "[Currency Value] Total contract value (TCV)"): run 2026-10-31, TCV $1,007.25 went THEN on > 1000 and ELSE on > 5000 (same live report; `equipment-purchase-approval-threshold`) | number operators |
| the request's status (`TicketStatus`) | `is` / `isNot` a status name; a status this workflow sets is compared with its compiled (lab-prefixed) name. "Request Status", a RequestStatusEnum, no caseSensitive (same lab). That the run compares the NAME is INFERRED until a run | Request Status / Request Status ID |
| approval outcome | `approved` | Is / Is not |
| Risk Assessment / Collect Data From an ID Validated (`<as>.validated`) | `is: true` or `is: false` (a JSON boolean; `if` only) | Is, Is not, Is empty, Is not empty (harvested 2026-10-24) |
| Verify Someone's Identity text outputs (`<as>.fullname`, `first_name`, `middle_name`, `last_name`, `nationality`, `sex`, `address`, `place_of_birth`, `type_of_id`) and a send's Envelope ID (`<as>.envelopeId`) | the text operators (`if` only) | text operators with Match casing (builder harvest 2026-11-02, lab zz-wb-builder-harvest); the identity step's dates are offered too, not harvested |
| a send's Envelope Status (`<as>.status`) | `is` completed, declined or voided (no casing flag); a `switch` on it too (harvest 2026-11-02) | Equal to, Not equal to, Contains, … Is empty, Is not empty (harvested 2026-10-24) |
| everything else | not written | — |

**Several conditions** (≤5, harvested): `{ "all": [c, c] }` is AND (one group); `{ "any": [c, { "all":
[c, c] }] }` is OR of groups — stored `Or[And[…], And[…]]`, exactly as the builder stores "A AND B OR
C". A rule name generated from many conditions is cut to the 100-character step-name limit.

Every operator the builder offers for text, numbers and dates is now written. **Un-merged rules:**
turning off "Merge true and false branches?" asks "Keep steps after this merge?" (move them to the
True branch, the False branch, or delete them). With steps after the rule, they left the main path.
So the compiler takes `merge: false` only on the workflow's LAST top-level step. It is stored as
the builder stores it there: `merge: false`, `branchesToMerge: []`, and no Path End anywhere
(lab `zz-branch-operators-2`).

## Scoping rules

- **Data made inside a merged branch is gone after the merge.** A form, a document, an agent's
  outputs, a send's status or an approval made inside a branch of an `if` or a `switch` cannot be used after the rule.
  Every rule this compiler writes merges. The guide says "variables and files generated inside a
  merged rule's branches are not available after the merge" ("Configure a Branching Rule"
  mnv1698169910928; "Configuration Details for Complex Branching Rules" jaf1716918359288). The compiler refuses such a reference and
  names the rule. Use the data inside its branch, or make it before the rule. **Proven in the builder
  (lab `zz-merge-scope`, 2026-10-24):** a Send Documents for Signature placed after the merge has its
  document picker disabled ("No available variables of this type."), while the same step inside the
  branch offers the document. A rule after the merge still offers the form fields made BEFORE the rule. Parallel lanes are not
  scoped: an approval made in one lane and branched on after the lanes rejoin imports and draws
  cleanly (`vendor-parallel-review`, WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md "Second batch").
- **Within a branch, `then` and `else` cannot see each other's data.**
- **A send carries the one document made since the last send.** A second waiting document is
  refused, and so is the same template twice. This is an IMPORT limit, not a product limit: the product
  sends up to 15 documents in one step (help con30310a57). The builder makes such a
  send (`unifiedDocuments`, WORKFLOW-BUILDER-WORKFLOWS.md), but no package with one imports, not even
  Docusign's own export of it (500 ERR_10999, 2026-10-24). Give each document its own `sign`.
- **Who exists when.** Under a launcher start (Link, Manual, API Human), the first step's participant
  is the starter. Every other participant needs an `invite` before their first step. Under an Event,
  Schedule, CLM, Agreement Desk or automated API start, everyone does. Once someone else acts, the starter needs
  `{ "invite": { "participant": "starter" } }` before their next step, and a `sign` counts as theirs.

## Text that takes merges

`{{x}}` (a form answer, `start.x`, a request field, `<agent>.<output>`) merges in: `email` subject and
body, `message` body, `createRequest` title, `changeTitle`, `agent` prompt, a `confirm` TITLE and an
`invite` SUBJECT. The last two were harvested 2026-10-25 (lab `zz-text-merges`) and are stored as the
editor's document with a mention. It is REFUSED in the `invite` headline and button text, `sign` subject/message and `approval`. A `confirm`
description (≤300 characters, ≤50 variables) and an `invite` message (≤50 variables) take variables since
2026-10-29 (harvested on lab dabd08db, run-proven: the confirmation read "Thanks ZZ Lab Reviewer…" and the invite
email "Hello ZZ Lab Reviewer…"). Those would
print the braces, and no harvest has stored a variable there yet.

**Bold:** `**x**` compiles to a text node with the editor's bold mark (`marks: [{ type: "bold" }]`). It was proven
2026-10-26 (lab `zz-message-bold-compiled`): imported, the request message's editor showed the line bold, and
the builder's own Bold button stores the same mark. Proven in a request message; Send an Email uses the same
editor document. A request `message` also takes a `subject` (merges and bold, like the body). Emoji are
plain text.

## Checked against Docusign's help (2026-10-28)

- The compiler refuses more than 15 document steps (generate, esign, getDocument) in one workflow ("a total of
  up to 15 documents in a single workflow"); a starting variable name over 150 characters or a default over
  4000 (ogx1738026109020); an instance-name merge that is a person (otm1696972807664).
- `npm run workflow:check` warns (`help:`) when an approval's outcome is never branched on (a rejection blocks
  the run, con3a9658b0), when a workflow has more than 40 steps (otm1696972807664), and when a status-changed
  start has no request-type condition (it fires for every request type).
- **An account holds at most 30 LIVE request statuses** (deleted ones don't count). An import that would
  pass 30 creates statuses up to the cap, then fails with 500 ERR_10999 "Failed to import request status …:
  400" (the lab account 2026-10-28: 25 live — 16 of the owner's own and 9 "Fontara: …" — plus 5 created,
  then the 6th refused). So statuses are REUSED, never created: library specs name the account's own shared
  statuses (Pending Approval, Legal Review, Business Review, In Progress, Ready for Signature), and a verify or deploy carries each with its LIVE id and name (`existingStatuses`), which the
  importer reuses — 0 created (probe B, lab `zz-status-reuse`, 2026-10-28). Naming a live id WITHOUT carrying it
  fails: the importer strips the reference ("reconfigure the step", probe A). workflow:check warns over 5.
- Not checked, worth knowing in a demo: a workflow with Add Parallel Branches cannot retry a step
  (tsk9f5912a8), and a Link or API (human) start cannot be replayed (task-6406) — start a new instance.

**The send drawer shows "Participant: Select" for a compiled send.** Its "Confirm recipient details" step
shows "Select" in each recipient's Participant box for a compiled package, both for the run-proven
`nda-request-to-signature` and under a request start (control inspects 2026-10-28). It is how the drawer
displays an imported mapping, not a missing one: those sends deliver to the mapped participants (whether
re-applying the drawer by hand keeps the mapping is untested).

## Deliberately not supported, and why

| Feature | Why |
|---|---|
| Branch on an identity step's other outputs (risk scores, Participant risk — offered as free text) | Not harvested for a rule. Validated and Envelope Status ARE supported since 2026-10-24 |
| An un-merged rule anywhere but last | Un-merging moves or deletes the steps after it in the builder; only the last-step shape is harvested |
| A Multi Branch with some branches un-merged | Not harvested |
| A send of several documents | An IMPORT limit, not a product limit: Import Workflow refuses it (500 ERR_10999), even Docusign's own export, while the builder allows up to 15 documents per send ([con30310a57](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=yff1696971835267&topicId=con30310a57-3e53-40f2-a7f0-d9e099874eaa.html)). Add the second document in the canvas after import if a demo needs one envelope |
| "Needs to view" for a template role | Not harvested. "Receives a copy" IS compiled (`sign` … `copies` [roles]): the builder enables the action only for a template role with NO fields; it is stored as `recipients.carbonCopies[]` and the config instance's `recipientType: "carboncopy"` (harvested 2026-10-29, lab 6212f531; import-proven, not run) |
| A send's recipients in the drawer after import | FIXED after import (src/workflow-repoint.ts, run by workflow-verify and deploy-scenario): the importer re-points a document step's template id but not its `<templateId>_<recipientId>` keys (step input and config instance), so the send drawer's step 3 opened with Participant "Select" for every role. The keys are rewritten to the new template id and saved as Save Draft does (PUT definition + POST configInstances). Proven 2026-10-29: lab 96cbead1's drawer shows each role's participant, its canvas has no error, and a run delivered the envelope (lab inbox) |
| Direct signing by a first signer who is not the starter | The harvest's first signer was another participant and the builder accepted it, but who can sign in session then is unproven |
| SMS/WhatsApp, envelope custom fields (account-wide), per-recipient messages, "Apply from an envelope template" | Not harvested (per-recipient fields were not found by the harvest script) |
| Variables in the invite headline/button and the send subject/message | Each editor offers "/" variables, but no harvest has stored one there yet. Supported: a confirmation title and description (description ≤300 characters, ≤50 variables), an invite subject (≤3 variables, kfx1698167344720) and message (≤50 variables; the description and the message run-proven on lab 84f8d6c8, commit e3eee8e0), and a generated document's title (`documentName`, harvested) |
| Confirmation message types "End of participant's tasks" (and "… more tasks later", "… maybe more tasks later") | Offered (lab `zz-text-merges`); the compiler writes a custom message, and the builder stores that as "Write Custom Message" |
| Agent "act as publisher / starter" | Not offered: the drawer shows only Choose agent and Set up prompt under a Link start (lab `zz-agent-act-as-base`, 2026-10-24), a human API start (`zz-reprobe-agent-api`, 2026-10-28), a Manual start and an Agreement Desk request start (labs `zz-agent-manual`, `zz-agent-request`, 2026-11-01). The help (task-1036) describes an "Agent permissions" step this builder does not show. |
| Send an Email CC/BCC | The product has none: lab `zz-email-cc` found only "Add Recipient" (the help agent's lead was wrong) |
| Phone and Currency starting variables | Compiled for an API start since 2026-10-29: read by part, `start.<name>.countryCode / number / extension` and `start.<name>.doubleValue / currencyCode`. The trigger is called with `{ countryCode, number, extension }` / `{ currencyCode, doubleValue }` (help ogx; run-proven on lab b0221dbd: "Amount 5300000 USD, phone +1 4155550100"). Link starts are not harvested |
| Connected-app steps other than Read from / Writeback to Salesforce and Read from Stripe (Google Drive, SharePoint, Box, HubSpot, …), workflow branding. Use Data from a Table is built as `lookup` (its CSV is uploaded to the account first) | Each depends on something in the account that does not travel in a package (a connection, a document, a playbook, an installed app) |
| Add Connected Forms | Early Access |

Refused as product limits (guards): the compiler names the workaround instead of "unknown key".

| Spec asks for | Refusal names |
|---|---|
| A `loop`, `forEach` or `repeat` step | No loop step: one run per item (an API start called per item, or Bulk Send) |
| A `goto` or `loopBack` step | No loop back: each round is a new run, chained by a `workflow-completed` event start |
| A `compute`, `calculate`, `expression`, `formula` or `setVariable` step | No calculation step: ask on the form, or compute in an agent step (text output) or a document template formula |
| `approval.mode` other than `any` / `all`, or `approval.quorum` | No k of n: one approval per approver (in a parallel step), then a branch on their `approved` results |
| An `approval` under a start that is not a request | The approver decides on a web form: a form step by the approver, then an `if` on its answer |
| `schedule.repeat` other than once / daily / weekly / monthly, or `schedule.interval` / `every` | One scheduled workflow per run date, repeat `once` |
| `owner` from a workflow value (`<form>.<key>`, an agent or lookup output) | The Assign Owner picker lists only Pick a user and Request Submitter (drawer, lab 2026-10-31): branch on the value and name each owner |
| `getDocument` `label` / `documentLabel` | Get Document from a Request has one mode, the document template that generated the document (drawer, lab 2026-10-31) |
| `createRequest` `map` into a party field | Field mapping lists no party field (drawer, lab 2026-10-31): map the name into a text intake field, or let the requester add the party |

## Publishing (a person's step)

An import lands as a draft; publishing is the account owner's step. What Review & Publish sends (Workflow Builder's
internal `aow-manage` API, captured 2026-11-23):

1. **The check:** `POST …/workflowDefinitions/{id}/publish?preRunCheck=true&cancelRunningInstances=false` with
   `{"locale": "en"}`. It never publishes. Read the answer's `responseType`, not the HTTP status:
   - `NeedConsent` with a consent URL: the publisher opens it once and authorizes the application senders;
   - `AllCheckPassed`: ready. With an agent step the answer also carries `disclaimer: {text, version}`: the words
     the builder shows under a required **Confirm** box. A workflow without an agent step has no disclaimer.
2. **The publish:** `POST …/publish?preRunCheck=false&cancelRunningInstances=false&disclaimerAcknowledged=true&disclaimerVersion=<version>`
   with `{"locale": "en"}`. The tick is those two query values and nothing else; without them a workflow with an agent
   step answers `ERR_10807`. Publishing is asynchronous (`publishing` for 5–8 s, then `active`).

- **Show Docusign's own words, and get an explicit "I agree" from the person who publishes.** Show `disclaimer.text`
  as the check returned it (never a summary or your own wording), leave the agreement unticked, send the `version`
  you showed, and record who agreed. Never acknowledge the disclaimer for anyone.
- **`isPreRunCheck=true` is not a dry run**: on a workflow whose checks all pass it publishes (2026-11-06). Use
  `preRunCheck=true`, as the builder does.
- Unpublish is the same URL with `preRunCheck=false&cancelRunningInstances=true` and the body
  `{"deploymentStatus": "UnPublish"}`; without that body it publishes again.

## Where Docusign's help and this compiler disagree (docs-research, 2026-10-29)

The help wins unless a lab run proved otherwise. Run-proven exceptions are kept and marked.

- **From a Schedule**: the help never names this start (ztb1727892686033). The compiler builds it from the lab harvest; treat it as lab-only.
- **Events**: the help lists ten events. The compiler also builds an eleventh, Insights available (AM task-4459).
- **Request submitted** also fires when a request is changed to this type (tsk253a6185); see the start table.
- **Several documents in one send**: the product allows 15; an import refuses it (see the gaps table).
- **Send under an Agreement Desk start**: the help sends as the request owner or submitter after a one-time consent (con85f610e6). The compiler sends as the workflow's creator with `by` (run-proven), and has no submitter option yet.
- **Agent permissions**: the help shows them under Manual and API starts (task-1036). The lab did not see them under Link or human API starts. Manual is not probed.
- **Send Request Message subject**: the help documents only a system subject (tskcfabdfc0). The compiler writes a harvested `subject`.
- **Create a Request, automatic mode**: the product creates the request with unmapped required fields blank (task-7234). The compiler refuses that on purpose.
- **Prepare Document Template review**: the help offers manual review only under Manual and API starts, with sender fields (cra1749229692878). The Link-start behaviour here is run-proven but is not the documented case.

## Done screens and request-filled documents (2026-10-29)

- **Done screens.** When a person has finished all their steps in a session and the run then waits on someone else (a send for signature, an approval, an invite, an agent, another person's step), the compiler adds a Show a Confirmation Screen for them right after their last step ("You're done … you can close this page"). Without it their page stayed on a loading screen (a2 run f1c56f44; again on Test 2 2026-11-07, run 575edf7a, until the rule learned that a send with `documents` is the creator's automatic send, not the starter's draft). A later step of theirs in the same session, or a confirm the spec already has, means no screen; a re-invite starts a new session. `"doneScreens": false` turns it off; `{ "title", "description" }` replaces the text. A confirm completes as it shows, so the run goes on (lab 26a9956f: the deal desk rep saw it after Prepare Document Template, and the send then went out).
- **A template field filled from the request** (request start): `fill: { <field>: "request.<intake key>" }`, `request.<key>.currencyCode` for a currency's code, or a custom field's name (`C_…`). A dropdown is filled by the request's option VALUE, which the run matches against the template's option values, so every value the request offers must be a template `optionValues` entry (the compiler refuses otherwise). A provision with several properties (Renewal) does NOT reach the run (its value is not in the trigger's inputs), so a custom intake field is used instead. Proven 2026-10-29 (lab 26a9956f): the deal desk preview opened with Plan, Renewal, Negotiated position, Currency and Overage rate all filled. A request **date** (a custom Date field) into a template date field is proven 2026-10-31 on a second lab account (the drawer lists it under Variables from Workflow Start by its label; a submitted 03/13/2027 showed on the preview; [live report](../assets/workflows/live/legal-hold-notice-on-request-run.json)). A request **currency amount** (`request.<currency key>`, read as its `doubleValue`) into a number field is proven too (run 2026-10-31: the drawer lists it as "<field> (Double Value)" and writes the template field's number format N2; $1,003.25 showed as 1,003.25 on the preview; [live report](../assets/workflows/live/contract-value-amendment-on-request-run.json)). Library specs: `legal-hold-notice-on-request`, `contract-value-amendment-on-request`. A dropdown whose document must print longer text than the request's key (an entity's legal description): the template's `optionValues` are the request's keys (`"Fontara, Inc.": "Fontara_Inc"`) and the text is printed by one rule per option, never by `{{field}}` (the template validator refuses that: it would print the key). The same holds under a status start narrowed to the type. RUN 2026-11-01 on the lab account under a status start, unattended: the document printed the entity's legal description and not its key ([live report](../assets/prompt-corpus/live/desk-status-changed-generate.json); corpus `desk-status-changed-generate`, template `mutual-nda-from-request`).

## Platform changes checked 2026-10-29 (docs-research avoid-issues)

- **API-only templates** (eSignature 26.3.02, Early Access): templates with "non-standard JSONata" or classic syntax get a syntax icon and cannot be used in Workflow Builder or Agreement Desk. Our Word `formula` fields are JSONata ($sum, $number, $replace). The deployed order form that uses them shows no restriction (the template API reports only `isAceGenTemplate: true`), and Workflow Builder generated it on 2026-10-29. Re-check when the feature leaves Early Access.
- **Currency**: a Read step now types Currency natively. The request Currency fill writes `usd` because the org's Salesforce multi-currency is off (no CurrencyIsoCode). Read the code from Salesforce if multi-currency is turned on.
- **Request message attachments**: a request message sends at most 20 attachments, 25 MB in total. `attachDocuments` on a request with more sends only part of them.
- **Multiple documents per send**: the Send step is redesigned for mixed documents (production 2026-11-05; on a second lab account since 2026-11-01). `sign` … `documents` compiles the redesigned shape; re-test the old shape's refusal on the lab account on or after 2026-11-05.
- **Apply template settings** on a standalone document in the redesigned Send step: the step stays InProgress and the template's signers are listed twice (2 tries, a second lab account, 2026-11-01). Not compiled. Re-test 2026-11-09 (the lab account, lab 4ae20d1a): the drawer ('Apply template setting' in the document's ⋮ menu) lists each signer once and stores `appliedTemplates[<file variable>]` with the template's anchored tabs, but the step's `input.recipients.signers` holds every role three times and stays InProgress. Still not compiled: it needs a run, which needs a person to submit the web form.
- **Email sender name** (lab 54576da9, 2026-10-29): the builder still writes `sender_name: "Docusign Maestro"`, `sender_alias: "Maestro"` for Send an Email (`MaestroEmailConfigurator`) and Set Up Invite, and neither drawer offers a sender name. Recipients see "Docusign Workflows" as the sender. The only change is that an invite is now saved with `templateVersion: 2`; the compiler writes that too (a run delivered both emails).
- **Multi Branch AND/OR** (eSignature 26.3.01 release notes): not in this demo account's builder yet. On lab 7825438f (2026-10-29) a branch still offers one value with a fixed "equals" (options: Move down, Delete). The compiler keeps equals-only `switch`; use nested `if` rules for AND/OR.
- **Status colours**: Agreement Desk has 10 (success, warning, alert, neutral, purple, blue, gold, cactus, maroon, teal; its own bundle). Any other value displays as success, so the compiler refuses it. Which one to pick: Status colours by meaning, above.
